key_insight: A finite element model couples a pure fluid to a deformable poroelastic medium while capturing interface dissipation that significantly affects system behavior.
engineering_relevance: The formulation supports simulations of fluid interacting with deformable porous structures where interface transport and traction transfer influence the response.
method: Use mixture theory and an arbitrary Lagrangian–Eulerian formulation for both domains.
Allow discontinuous fluid velocity and pressure while maintaining a globally continuous displacement field.
Enforce normal filtration-velocity continuity with a Lagrange multiplier and incorporate dissipative momentum jump conditions.
evidence_signal: Manufactured-solution tests showed satisfactory convergence, a benchmark analytical solution was reproduced, and a sample problem compared inert and fully dissipative interfaces.
watch_item: Predictions depend strongly on the chosen interface model, so its dissipative behavior requires careful physical justification.
paper_title: A Finite Element Model for Fluid--Poroelastic Structure Interaction with Dissipative Interface
